setting: A fictional job interview for a {{role}} role.

presentation.situation: You are interviewing for a {{role}} role with {{name}}. {{name}} wants a real example of {{focus}}. Use your own experience.
presentation.opening: Welcome. Thanks for coming in. Could you tell me about a time when you dealt with {{focus}}?

brief.you_are: You are a candidate in a job interview.
brief.situation: You are interviewing for a {{role}} role with {{name}}. {{name}} wants a real example of {{focus}}. Use your own experience.
brief.task: Give a relevant real example, explain the situation, what you did and the result, and answer confidently.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} has a specific, relevant example, and knows what you did and what happened.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are a candidate in a job interview.
goals: Give a relevant real example, explain the situation, what you did and the result, and answer confidently.

card.want: Evidence that you can do this job.
card.attitude: Polite and attentive, and probes vague answers.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Never supply the details of the example

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: The candidate's examples come from their own experience. {{name}} knows only what the candidate says.
The role involves a lot of {{focus}}.

objectives.evidence: The learner offers a relevant real example, and sets the context.
alternatives: In my last job, a customer was unhappy about a late order.

objectives.description: Explain your actions and the result
objectives.evidence: The learner explains their own actions and the result.
alternatives: I called the customer and fixed it, and they stayed with us.

objectives.description: Connect your strengths to the role
objectives.evidence: The learner connects this to the role with confidence.
alternatives: I can bring that same approach to this role.

examples: In my last job, a customer was unhappy about a late order.
I called the customer and fixed it, and as a result they stayed with us.
I can bring that same approach to this role.

signals: \b(?:in my (?:last|previous|current)|at my|when i|last year|one time|for example|situation|project)\b
opportunity: Can you think of a specific time?
Tell me about one real situation.
beats.orient: It's a job interview. Tell me about one real time from your own experience. Start with: In my last job.
fallback: Tell me about one real situation.
Can you think of a specific time?

beats.goal: Hear personal action and the result.
beats.orient: Now tell me what you did, and what happened. Use: I did, and: the result was.

signals: \b(?:i can|i will|i have|i would bring|this role|this job|i bring)\b
opportunity: Why does that matter for this role?
How would that help you here?
beats.orient: Now connect your example to this job. Start with: I can bring that to this role because.
fallback: How would that help you here?
Why does that matter for this role?

closing_line: Thank you. That is exactly what I wanted to hear about.

o1.micro_lesson: Choose one real situation. Start with when and where.
o1.model: In my last job, a customer was unhappy about a late order.

o2.good: Your own actions, then a real result.
o2.micro_lesson: Say 'I' for what you did, and end with the result.
o2.model: I called the customer and fixed it, and as a result they stayed with us.

o3.good: A plain statement of what you can do.
common_mistakes: Undermining yourself: I am not sure, but
o3.micro_lesson: Say: I can, and how it helps this job.
o3.model: I can bring that same approach to this role.
